source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Place the drainage system on the bed at chest level.","B":"Keep the drainage system upright and below the client's chest.","C":"Raise the system above the chest during repositioning.","D":"Clamp the tube routinely during transport."}}
source_row.rationale: Keeping the chest drainage system upright and below the chest supports drainage and reduces the risk of fluid backflow. Option B is correct. Placing the system at or above chest level or routinely clamping the tube can create complications.
source_row.source_detail: Chest drainage management: keep the drainage system upright and below chest/insertion-site level to facilitate dependent drainage and prevent backflow; avoid unnecessary clamping and dependent tubing loops.
